parsed.doc_summary: G.L. c. 40P, § 4 generally bars Massachusetts cities and towns from enacting, maintaining or enforcing rent control, with a narrow voluntary, compensated exception. This means no local rent control applies in MA cities.

rules.title: State bar on local rent control
rules.requirement: Cities and towns in Massachusetts may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally compensated regulation for owners of 10 or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.key_value: state bar on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in the document.
rules.exemptions: Exception for cities/towns accepting the chapter: voluntary compliance after six months, owners must own 10+ units, fair market rent not exceeding $400, municipality compensates owners from general funds.
rules.interaction: Bars local rent control by cities such as Boston and Cambridge.

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts has no rent control cap; state law prohibits local rent control, so there is no local rent cap in MA cities such as Boston and Cambridge.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind
